title: Tupac trial: What you need to know
description:
Rapper Tupac Shakur is one of the most influential music artists ever - with musicians such as Kendrick Lamar, Justin Bieber and Drake citing him as a major inspiration. His career was cut short in 1996 when he was killed in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas - but now, nearly three decades later, a man is going on trial, accused of his murder. He’s called Duane "Keffe D" Davis - he has pled not guilty and denies all allegations.

So, what we can expect from the trial? And how is Tupac’s music continuing to influence hip-hop, decades after his murder?

We speak to culture journalist Ivie Ani, who’s based in New York, to learn more about the impact Tupac has had on music today. We also hear from Tupac fans that have discovered his legacy in the years since his death - and from Anoushka Mutanda-Dougherty, host of the BBC’s Fame Under Fire podcast. She is in Las Vegas covering the rapper’s murder trial.

You can follow the trial by listening to the Fame Under Fire podcast here: https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/m0030zm4

Instagram: @bbcwhatintheworld Email: whatintheworld@bbc.co.uk WhatsApp: +44 330 12 33 22 6 Presenter: Hannah Gelbart Producers: William Lee Adams, Chelsea Coates and Emma-Louise Amanshia Editors: Verity Wilde
summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討已故著名饒舌歌手 Tupac Shakur 在 1996 年於拉斯維加斯遭槍殺近 30 年後的謀殺案審判進展，以及他對嘻哈音樂與文化的深遠影響。被告 Duane "Keffe D" Davis 在 2023 年被起訴後否認控罪，案情關鍵在於其自傳與公開訪談內容。文化記者 Ivie Ani 與 BBC 記者 Anoushka Mutanda-Dougherty 探討了該案背景、檢警證據，以及 Tupac 作為首位推出雙 CD 嘻哈專輯與獄中發行專輯的先驅，如何持續啟發 Kendrick Lamar 等當代音樂人。
summaryEn: This episode of What in the World examines the murder trial surrounding legendary rapper Tupac Shakur nearly 30 years after his death in a 1996 Las Vegas drive-by shooting, as well as his lasting legacy in hip-hop culture. Host Hannah Gelbart speaks with BBC reporter Anoushka Mutanda-Dougherty about suspect Duane "Keffe D" Davis, who was charged in 2023 after making self-incriminating claims in podcasts and a memoir, though he now claims parts of those accounts were fictionalized. Culture journalist Ivie Ani also joins to discuss Tupac's groundbreaking musical milestones—such as pioneering double-disc hip-hop releases—and how his artistry and socio-political activism continue to inspire modern artists like Kendrick Lamar and Future.
